profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 41 (Stream Data Centers missing-address campaign): found this campus actually comprises two buildings, one of which was sold to LightEdge in January 2024, and declined to assign a specific street number given no way to confirm which building this generic row represents, flagged the rows own operator attribution as possibly needing re-verification, sourced and dated the companys Apollo majority acquisition (completed November 3, 2025) which the registry had previously recorded without a citable source. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999. This session sourced and dated the companys recent ownership change, previously recorded without a citation: per Apollo Global Managements own press releases, Apollo announced a deal to acquire a majority stake in Stream Data Centers in August 2025 and completed that acquisition on November 3, 2025, with Principal Asset Management separately acquiring a minority stake through a Principal managed fund, and Streams own management team retaining a minority stake while continuing to lead operations. The companys own site and Apollos press materials describe more than 20 to 27 campuses delivered, a 4 plus gigawatt active development pipeline, and more than 90 percent of capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers. Primary named markets include Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Minneapolis, Phoenix, and San Antonio. This specific row, recorded simply as StreamData Center in Chaska, MN, could not be confidently matched to a specific building this session, and a material complication was found rather than a simple gap. The operators own Minneapolis locations page, fetched fresh this session, describes two adjacent buildings at this campus: MSPA1, also called Minneapolis II, at 1706 West Creek Lane, Chaska, MN 55318, 56,000 square feet, fully leased and still operated by Stream, and Minneapolis I, at 1708 West Creek Lane, Chaska, MN 55318, 75,800 square feet, which that same operator page states was sold in January 2024. Independent Data Center Dynamics trade press and multiple aggregators, datacenterHawk, DataCenterMap, Baxtel, and datacenters.com, corroborate that sale, reporting the buyer as LightEdge, backed by GI Partners, with aggregator listings for 1708 West Creek Lane now rebranded LightEdge Minneapolis I accordingly. This registry row carries only generic coordinates and a generic name, with no building letter or roman numeral to disambiguate it from either 1706 or 1708, both of which sit on the same short street. Given one of the two candidate buildings changed operators in January 2024, asserting either specific street number here risks misattributing either a still current Stream building as sold, or a now sold building as still Stream, so no specific address is asserted for this row. A future researcher with access to precise parcel level geocoding could likely resolve which of the two buildings this specific row represents, and should also re-verify whether this rows own operator field of Stream remains correct once that is known.

reading.body:
This registry row represents a campus in Chaska, Minnesota that comprises two adjacent buildings on West Creek Lane, one still operated by Stream and one sold to LightEdge in January 2024. The research notes describe the ambiguity precisely: the row's generic coordinates and address do not specify which building it represents, and resolving that ambiguity requires parcel-level geocoding or re-verification of the operator field itself. Until that resolution, this row cannot be confidently attributed to either Stream or LightEdge, and cannot be matched to a specific published capacity figure.

The state context shows Minnesota has 13 mapped data center facilities and only 2 with published capacity figures totaling 10 MW. This row ranks third in the state by published megawatts, but that ranking applies only if the row's specifications are correct and unambiguous. The state context does not clarify what published power specifications this row itself carries, and the ambiguity over which building it represents means no capacity figure can be safely attributed to either operator at this location.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI, the material fact is the unresolved identity of the facility. The research status is marked complete, but completion here means documenting a genuine ambiguity rather than resolving it. Until the specific building and its current operator are confirmed through parcel-level geocoding or direct re-verification, this row cannot inform decisions about either Stream's capacity in Minnesota or LightEdge's footprint. A future researcher should treat this as a flagged case requiring ground-truth verification before it can be read as a published specification.
